title: Gen-2 shared definitions
description: Identifiers, hashes, timestamps and enumerations shared by every gen-2 schema. Prefix-typed IDs make cross-wiring (an operation ID where an invocation ID belongs) a validation error instead of a silent join.

sha256.description: 'sha256:' + 64 lowercase hex digits. Two kinds, never mixed (Astra ruling R1; gen2/store/README.md 'Hashing contract'): a logical hash is SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 JCS serialization of a JSON value (canonicalization jcs-rfc8785/1; content_hash excludes only itself, request_fingerprint excludes only submitted_at); a byte digest is SHA-256 over retained bytes exactly as received/staged (raw provider responses, artifacts) and is never computed over a canonicalized re-serialization. Both are computed by gen2/core/canonical.py.

commit_hash_contract.description: The canonicalization and request-fingerprint contracts a commit receipt's hashes were computed under (Astra 0a ruling R1: versioned, and frozen in 0b before durable identities or replay fixtures exist). Recorded on every commit receipt; the only admitted values are the frozen ones (gen2/core/canonical.py CANONICALIZATION, FINGERPRINT_CONTRACT). A new contract is a new version here and in the DDL, never an edit in place.

logical_hash_contract.description: The canonicalization contract a receipt's logical (JCS) hashes were computed under, for receipts that carry logical hashes but no request fingerprint (decision receipts: spec_hash). Frozen as commit_hash_contract is.

timestamp.description: UTC instant, RFC 3339 with a literal Z, naming a real calendar instant. The pattern is only a shape pre-filter (it admits February 31); calendar validity is the `date-time` format, checked by gen2/core/instants.py:is_utc_instant — the one validator, applied at the router's schema-validation boundary and registered by tools/check_gen2_schemas.py (Astra 0a review A11). The store keeps router-validated text and does not re-validate.

topic_id.description: '<fleet_id>:<topic slug>'. Fleet-prefixed so Fleet A/B topics with similar names are never merged (design review §4).

local_id.description: An identifier stable within one topic (obligation, facet, criterion, rule, entry).

revision.description: A document revision number; revisions start at 1. Identity numbers are bounded BY VALUE to 2^53-1 (Astra re-review RA8): JSON Schema treats 9007199254740992, 9007199254740992.0 and 9007199254740992e0 alike as the integer 2^53, so `maximum` refuses all three; larger identities travel as strings (gen2/core/canonical.py identity_integer states the same bound).

state_revision.description: The router's optimistic-concurrency counter for a topic; starts at 0. Bounded by value like revision (RA8).

generation.description: A lease or publication generation (or other identity counter): strictly increasing per topic. Bounded by value like revision (RA8).

artifact_ref.description: An immutable, content-addressed artifact staged by trusted station code in the protected spool. Location derives from the hash; agents never choose a destination path (design review §5).

brief_ref.description: An operator-confirmed Intake Brief version (flow S1: confirmation is an explicit, versioned act; document: intake-brief.schema.json). The store binds this triple to the topic's confirmed intake_briefs row and to the brief_confirmation decision that confirmed it (task 0b).

admission_context.description: What an invocation was admitted under, pinned for its whole life (Astra 0a review A4; INVARIANTS C-12). contract/1: scientific work under an approved Contract v2 revision. pre-contract/1: S2 scoping / S3 contract drafting (invocation kinds discovery, delegate, research_pass only) under an operator-confirmed brief, admissible only while the topic has never had an approved contract; it can finalize, but it can never earn a research ordinal or write rows that require the approved protocol. Versioned so a later context is a new const, never a reinterpretation.

observed_count.description: A count that may be unobserved or only partly observed. Unknown is a distinct state with a reason, never 0 (invariant RG-U; flow §4.3). Partial (A11/RG-4): the records actually observed are kept and counted, the value is a lower bound, and the reason says why the rest is missing — it never supports exhausted coverage, negative evidence or saturation.

access_tier.description: Ordered: bibliographic < abstract < full_text < reproduced. Different checks, not interchangeable 'verified' flags (flow S4 step 8; design review §8).

candidate_unit.description: The four units evidence accounting keeps distinct (flow S4 step 2; adjudication (b)7).

coverage_state.description: Gateway coverage vocabulary with its narrow meanings (gateway/docs/STATION-CONTRACT.md §2), plus 'unknown' for lost telemetry — design review §9: missing observations become acknowledged unknowns, never ignored.

invocation_kind.description: Every execution kind shares one lifecycle (BOUNDARIES.md Station supervisor; invariant RG-2). Decision-provider calls are made inside an invocation, not as a kind of their own.

invocation_state.description: Allowed transitions are listed in docs/gen2/INVARIANTS.md L-1 and enforced by the invocations trigger in gen2/store/schema.sql.

completion_outcome.description: Distinct recorded outcomes (flow S7). A resource stop is never relabeled as saturation.

decision_class.description: Decision classes named in the flow doc. Initial rollout exercises only screening (shadow) and method_selection (advisory) — flow §5.

authority_level.description: shadow: logged, never shown or acted on. advisory: a recommendation a person or the primary disposes of. qualified: the router's policy may commit a reversible action; requires a qualification reference for this exact DecisionSpec (flow §2).

sink.description: Physical publication sinks, named as such — never 'GraphRAG' (flow S8 item 2).
